movie.title: Big Chicken: A Fast Food Conspiracy
movie.originalTitle: Big Chicken: A Fast Food Conspiracy
movie.overview: In a bold 28-day experiment, comedian Mo Gilligan tours the UK and US on a fried chicken diet to uncover the impact of the craving — and industry behind it.

aiEnrichment.summary_one_sentence: Comedian Mo Gilligan embarks on a 28-day cross-Atlantic fried chicken diet to uncover the fast-food industry's cultural hold and health impacts.
aiEnrichment.summary_short: In this engaging documentary, comedian Mo Gilligan takes on an intense 28-day challenge of eating strictly fried chicken across the UK and the US. Along the way, he investigates the irresistible cravings driving the global fast-food craze and the massive corporate machinery fueling it. Combining humor with investigative journalism, the film exposes how fast food shapes modern diets, communities, and public health.
aiEnrichment.summary_long: Driven by his personal love for fast food and a curiosity about its cultural dominance, comedian Mo Gilligan sets out on an eye-opening 28-day experiment. Committing to an all-fried-chicken diet, Mo travels across major cities in both the United Kingdom and the United States to sample iconic local spots and major global chains. As the physical and mental toll of the restrictive diet begins to set in, he consults with medical professionals, nutritionists, and addiction experts to monitor his changing health parameters. Beyond his personal physical transformation, Mo investigates the aggressive marketing tactics and scientific formulations that fast-food corporations use to make fried chicken so addictively convenient. He dives into the socio-economic factors that make fast food a primary dietary choice in lower-income urban communities. Through insightful interviews with industry insiders, food historians, and passionate everyday consumers, Mo uncovers the deep economic and psychological roots of our fast-food obsession. Ultimately, the documentary balances Mo's signature humor with a stark look at the consequences of industrial food production, leaving viewers with a deeper understanding of what really goes into their favorite quick meals.
aiEnrichment.synopsis: Big Chicken: A Fast Food Conspiracy follows popular comedian Mo Gilligan as he undertakes a 28-day experiment, consuming only fried chicken while traveling across the United Kingdom and the United States. Through a blend of humor, personal health tracking, and investigative field reporting, the film examines the powerful fast-food industry, the science behind food cravings, and the broader social and cultural impacts of cheap, accessible fast food.

story_structure.climax: The 28-day challenge culminates in a critical inflection point where the cumulative toll of the experiment intersects with unsettling revelations about the fast-food industry's aggressive marketing and production practices.
story_structure.conflict: As physical fatigue and dietary challenges set in, Mo faces the core dilemma: balancing the addictive appeal of convenient, comforting fast food against the systemic health, economic, and industrial realities driving the craze.
story_structure.resolution: Mo completes the trial and synthesizes his findings, offering a balanced reflection on consumer cravings, industry accountability, and the true cost behind the accessibility of fast-food chicken.
story_structure.introduction: Comedian Mo Gilligan sets out on a 28-day cross-continental experiment across the UK and US, consuming a strict fried chicken diet to examine why the fast-food staple commands such global cultural and culinary dominance.
story_structure.risingAction: Mo travels between major cities, consulting nutrition experts, fast-food insiders, and local communities while documenting the physical, mental, and economic impacts of living exclusively on ultra-processed chicken.
